To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) Obesity may be considered as a heritable trait and (2) Epigenetics is involved in the regulation of the risk for developing obesity and in the pathogenesis of obesity.
obesity is a complex disorder that is caused by the interplay between genetic, epigenetics and environmental factors.
epigenetic modifications are involved in the regulation of the expression of genes involved in the etiopathogenesis of obesity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genetic and epigenetic factors involved in obesity.
the identification of genetic risk variants for obesity, and their functional characterization, with a special focus on epigenetic mechanisms and the role of the brain in obesity.
the identification of genetic and epigenetic factors that predispose to obesity, and the elucidation of the underlying biological mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epigenetic mechanisms involved in obesity are not well characterized.
obesity results from a complex interplay of genetic and environmental factors, which are modulated by epigenetic regulation and which, in turn, are modulating the genetic risk for obesity.

the current knowledge on the genetics and epigenetics of obesity is far from complete, but that it is rapidly evolving and will provide important new insights into the pathophysiology of this major disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
epigenetic mechanisms may contribute to the etiology of common (multifactional) obesity through a combination of genetic, environmental and lifestyle factors.
epigenetics and genetics are two important players in the etiology and pathogenesis of obesity.
epigenetics is an essential factor in obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
epigenetics and genetics interact in a complex way and that the epigenetic mechanisms underlying obesity are still largely unknown.
the epigenetic regulation of gene expression plays a crucial role in the regulation and development of obesity.
the interplay between genetic and environmental factors is mediated through epigenetic regulation of gene expression, thus, highlighting the importance of epigenetic regulation in obesity.
